page: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-level virtual server powered by a shared AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. Running on the QEMU hypervisor, the instance provides 1 shared vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz alongside 2.0 GB of system memory. The underlying processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with broad instruction set support featuring AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) and hardware-accelerated cryptographic operations via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Storage is provided via a bundled 40 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering local high-speed disk access without requiring separate block storage attachments. The instance includes zero dedicated GPUs and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on modern network and compute configurations tailored for lean deployments.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread execution, placing in the top 25% of tested systems for stress-ng single-core performance at 2999.88. Single-threaded gzip compression reaches 24.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieves 12.27 GB/sec. However, multi-core capacity and aggregate throughput remain constrained by the single shared vCPU design, reflected in lower PassMark CPU, memory bandwidth, and static web serving scores. Text generation on small 135M language models yields 107.47 tokens per second.

Given its minimal hardware footprint and shared resource allocation, Hetzner Cloud cpx12 serves as a cost-efficient platform for lightweight background services, microservices, staging environments, low-traffic web applications, and small utility or development nodes.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx12 is an entry-level virtual machine offering 1 shared vCPU based on the AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 2.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a bundled 40 GB NVMe SSD for fast local read and write operations, with no attached GPUs. Hardware features include AVX-512 vector support and cryptographic acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the cpx12 exhibits strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng evaluations, although total multi-core capacity and uncached memory bandwidth reflect its single-thread shared boundary. Small-scale model inference maintains steady throughput for low-parameter workloads. Due to its lean physical footprint and shared CPU allocation, the cpx12 provides a budget-friendly option tailored for microservices, lightweight web servers, development environments, and low-intensity background utilities.
